messages:
raj-support: FYI — LedgerPay (dedicated, eu-west-1) opened a ticket: repeated 429s and elevated tail latency starting ~10:12 UTC. They attached runtime logs showing rapid KV cache evictions and auth retries.

raj-support: Log snippet:
```
ERROR 2026-09-23T10:12:34Z tenant=ledgerpay req_id=6f9c status=429 reason=KV_CACHE_PRESSURE evictions=324 free_kv_mem=1.2GiB kv_hit_rate=0.62
WARN  2026-09-23T10:12:35Z tenant=ledgerpay auth_retry=3 downstream_latency=320ms
```

raj-support: Customer says workload is long-context conversation bursts (avg ctx=12k tokens, some up to 20k). They noticed spike correlates with a specific org team sending sequences in parallel. Asked for immediate mitigation and credit consideration. :thinking:

sara-eng: looking at infra metrics now. Query: `rate(kv_evictions_total{tenant=\"ledgerpay\"}[1m])` shows a 10x jump 10:11->10:13. Also seeing heap fragmentation on the runtime host: `slab_free_percent` dropping to 6%.

sara-eng: @tom-sre, this smells like slow slab coalescing + lots of long ctx KV allocations. Autoscaler didn't add hosts because overall GPU utilization stayed <60% — this is memory-local pressure on the KV cache.

tom-sre: ack. Repro plan: can we run a synthetic load that mimics 12k-20k contexts at ~40 QPS from a single tenant? If we reproduce locally we can validate eviction thresholds and slab behavior. I'll try a small harness.

raj-support: customer gave an example payload we can use. I'll paste minimal repro curl for the API gateway (token scrubbed):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -d '{"model":"r-infer-3b","input": "<long prompt with ~12k tokens>", "max_tokens": 3000}'
```

sara-eng: quick mitigation options: 1) Increase tenant KV window memory (e.g., kv_cache_mb from 1024 -> 4096) for ledgerpay to reduce eviction churn; 2) enable short-term per-tenant slab compaction flag on the runtime; 3) enforce per-tenant concurrency limit to avoid a single tenant spawning many long-ctx concurrent requests.

tom-sre: I spun up the harness (script attached) and reproduced evictions locally within 90s. Eviction churn causes worker GC to stall ~200-400ms which then pushes request latencies and triggers API-level 429s when request queue hits SLO guardrails. Code snippet I used:
```python
# pseudocode
for i in range(50):
  send_long_ctx_request(tokens=12000)
  sleep(0.05)
```

alyssa-cs: LedgerPay is asking about billing — they saw a jump in billable tokens due to retries. They want a partial credit if this is platform throttling. Also they requested an ETA for a fix.

raj-support: I told them short-term we can try the kv_cache bump and a soft concurrency cap while we investigate. They asked if we can do it today.

sara-eng: I can flip a tenant-level kv_cache override for ledgerpay on the runtime config (non-disruptive). @deploy-bot can you schedule a config change for eu-west-1 runtime pool? We'll keep it under a 30-min maintenance window.

deploy-bot: scheduled: tenant override `ledgerpay.kv_cache_mb=4096` rolling apply to runtime-pool-eu-west-1 at 2026-09-23T11:05:00Z. No full process restart expected.

tom-sre: follow-ups: 1) run slab compaction patch on a canary host (low traffic) to measure fragmentation delta; 2) add a telemetry counter for `eviction_churn_ms` and correlate to 429s; 3) tweak autoscaler policy to consider KV memory pressure as a trigger (not just GPU util). I'll open PRs for 1 & 2 and a proposal doc for 3.

sara-eng: agree. Short-term action items assigned: Sara -> apply tenant override; Tom -> reproduce + compaction canary; Raj -> customer comms and billing triage with Alyssa.

alyssa-cs: I'll draft the customer note offering a one-time billing credit pending root cause. Will wait for confirmation after the mitigation.

raj-support: Customer update sent — keeping them in the loop. They accepted temporary kv bump and reduced concurrency for the next 24h.

tom-sre: preliminary canary results: slab_free_percent improved from 6% -> 22% after compaction on the canary host, eviction rate dropped ~70% under the synthetic load. Will run a 6h soak and post metrics. :thumbsup:

sara-eng: thanks all. We'll leave this thread for postmortem notes. If the soak is green, next steps are to: prod rollout of compaction, autoscaler change, and long-term allocator improvements to reduce fragmentation for long-context KV patterns.

raj-support: closing loop with ledgerpay; they're happy with plan and asked for a brief writeup once the postmortem is ready.

(reacts: :eyes: from alyssa-cs, :rocket: from sara-eng)
